column1: # Pfam families that model a cytoplasmic ribosomal protein of bacteria, archaea or eukaryotes:
# the whole protein, or a domain found only in that protein. Proteins use the universal
# nomenclature of Ban et al. 2014 (Curr Opin Struct Biol 24:165); families shared with other
# proteins (KOW, S4, KH, S1), ribosome biogenesis, modification, hibernation and rescue factors,
# and organelle-specific ribosomal proteins belong to other panels.
# Checked against the Pfam release behind pfam_predicates.tsv: Pfam-A.hmm (24,076 families)
# and Pfam-A.clans (30,134 families). Matching uses the accession, or the name when an
# Traditional names follow archaeal usage for u and e proteins (suffix p: bacterial-type numbering,
# e: eukaryotic-type, Ae: named after a eukaryotic "a" protein such as L35a) and bacterial usage
# for b proteins. The numbers differ between nomenclatures (eL33 is L35Ae; uL16 is L10e).
# Rows of another feature kind use kind:ID (a KEGG ortholog where Pfam lacks an archaeal family).
